worked: Federal (given, not tested): federal AGI = wages (person 0) 50,000.00 + wages (person 1) 40,000.00 = 90,000.00. Federal taxable income = 90,000.00 - standard deduction 31,500.00 = 58,500.00 (federal senior deduction ignored; Form PIT-1 takes only the federal line 12 amount, and no line for what the federal return subtracts after line 12). Form PIT-1, married filing jointly. Line 9 federal AGI 90,000.00. Line 10 0.00 (standard deduction taken). Line 11 additions 0.00. Line 12 federal standard deduction 31,500.00. Line 13 dependents 0.00. Line 14 0.00: federal AGI 90,000.00 is over the worksheet's printed ceiling 55,000.00 for this status, so the worksheet is not completed. Line 15 PIT-ADJ deductions and exemptions 0.00. Line 17 = 90,000.00 + 0.00 - 31,500.00 - 0.00 - 0.00 = 58,500.00. By the projection: state_agi = federal taxable income 58,500.00 = 58,500.00; less base deductions 0.00 gives 58,500.00. Line 18 tax, schedule as numbers: 1.5% x 8,000.00 = 120 + 3.2% x 17,000.00 = 544 + 4.3% x 25,000.00 = 1,075 + 4.7% x 8,500.00 = 399.5; total 2,138.5, to the cent 2,138.50. The table row over 58,400 to 58,500 gives 2,136; expected keeps the formula figure. Lines 19 to 21 0.00. Line 22 net New Mexico income tax 2,138.50.
